comment: One row for each behavior that the selected driver groundwork adds or holds: the
failed report close, the selected build, the C compiler, the brace range, the
imported uncalled bodies and the FIR ownership pass. The one stage runs every
targeted test, so the log of a row names each test that the mutant turns red.
The table runs in the Linux VM with the debug preset, in the slot that built it.
Configure that build with FORT_ENABLE_BOOTSTRAP0=OFF and a FORT_STAGE1_COMPILER, or
with the C-started chain. The analysis-after-build-mode mutant needs two edits, an
import and a call, so it is no row; the pre-transform group holds it by hand.
The md5 guard reads the product compiler that the build links.

stages.name: driver groundwork tests
stages.command: ctest --test-dir build/Linux/debug -R '^(fir|ownership_driver_groups|ownership_report_close)$' --output-on-failure; a=$?; python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --cc clang --target x86_64-linux-gnu --opt opt-18 fail/modules/024 fail/modules/025; b=$?; python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --cc clang --target x86_64-linux-gnu --opt opt-18 --check-json fail/modules/024 fail/modules/025; c=$?; echo "stage statuses: ctest $a lang $b lang-json $c"; exit $((a | b | c))

mutations.new:
bool closed = io.close(fd) || true;
    if (written && closed && rename(
mutations.what: a failed close of the temporary report still publishes it
a selected build skips the analysis that --check runs
a selected build with an incomplete proof still emits and starts --cc
a storage end at a closing brace has an empty range
violations of imported modules are not rendered
the FIR ownership pass writes its errors and exits 0
the FIR ownership pass ends with the verifier panic
the FIR ownership pass runs after the build-mode pass
an incomplete local proof of a FIR test function gives no error
